source: Technology Promotion Project to Increase Productivity Around Tonle Sap (TSTD — TA 7305-CAM), watermelon (ដំណាំឪឡឹក) technical training booklet, prepared by the project's agricultural techniques and extension officer in cooperation with East West Seed International, November 2016. Contact: livleanghy@gmail.com
text:
Before planting watermelon, clear the field of debris and remove all weeds so the soil surface is clean.

Plow the soil thoroughly and leave it exposed (fallow/sun-dried) for 10 to 15 days before the next step. This helps break down soil clods and reduce weed and pest pressure.

Plow the land a second time, using a cattle-drawn plow (គោក្រប៊ូ) or a walking tractor (គោយន្ត), to a working depth of 15 to 20 centimeters.

After plowing, farmers build raised planting beds/ridges (វេង). Bed width should be about 1 meter, with length adjusted to the field's shape and area, but a single bed should not exceed about 15 meters in length — longer beds make routine care such as watering and weeding more difficult.

Bed height differs by soil texture: on clay/heavier soils the bed height is roughly 15 to 30 centimeters, while on sandier or lighter soils the bed should be built higher, roughly 30 to 50 centimeters, to ensure adequate drainage.

Well-decomposed animal manure or composted soil should be worked into the bed at roughly 1 to 2 kilograms per meter of bed length, mixed thoroughly into the base soil before planting.

A soil or plastic mulch covering is recommended on top of the finished bed to reduce erosion/water runoff and to suppress weed growth.
